articles.originalTitle: Long-Awaited Le Large Finally Opens on Paris’s Idyllic Île Seguin - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Paris's New Contemporary Art Center Le Large Opens on Île Seguin
articles.excerpt: Le Large, a new contemporary art center on Île Seguin in western Paris, occupies a former industrial site. Designed by RCR Arquitectes, the venue opens with the exhibition Moteur Imaginaire.
articles.content: France's newest contemporary art center, Le Large, has opened on Île Seguin in Boulogne-Billancourt in the western suburbs of Paris. Once home to a Renault factory, the island is being transformed as part of a 450 million euro cultural development known as Pointe des Arts. Designed by Pritzker Prize-winning RCR Arquitectes, the building features a copper-colored anodized-aluminum facade with diamond-shaped elements. Operating with an estimated annual budget of 5 million euros, the center features flexible exhibition spaces capable of hosting either single large-scale shows or multiple simultaneous exhibitions. Around 40 percent of its public-facing spaces are free to enter. The institution operates on a hybrid model combining a nonprofit association and a commercial entity for private events. The inaugural exhibition, Moteur Imaginaire, is curated by Cecilia Alemani and brings together more than 100 works by 55 artists from 23 countries. Drawing on the island's industrial history, the display incorporates 50 pieces from the Renault collection alongside historical photographs, following a spatial layout that evokes automotive assembly lines.

articles.originalTitle: Thessaloniki’s 15th-century Hamza Bey Mosque reopens as arts centre after nearly 20-year conservation effort - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Thessaloniki's 15th-Century Hamza Bey Mosque Reopens as Arts Centre After Restoration
articles.excerpt: Commissioned in 1467, Thessaloniki's historic Hamza Bey Mosque has reopened as a cultural centre and exhibition space following a two-decade conservation project supported by the European Recovery Fund.
articles.content:
The 15th-century Hamza Bey Mosque in Thessaloniki reopened as an exhibition space and cultural centre following nearly two decades of conservation and restoration work. Commissioned in 1467 by the daughter of Ottoman admiral Hamza Bey, the building was later expanded in the 16th century. Following damage from fires and earthquakes, it was rebuilt in 1620 and subsequently served various functions after the 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey.

The site came under the protection of the Greek Ministry of Culture in 2006, with structural stabilisation beginning in 2007. The final phase of conservation, supported by the European Recovery Fund, took place between 2024 and 2026. The historic site is now managed by the Metropolitan Organisation of Museums of Visual Arts of Thessaloniki. The inaugural exhibition features black-and-white photographs by Pete Marifoglou documenting the city's modernization between 1960 and 1980. The project forms part of a broader urban program initiated by Culture Minister Lina Mendoni.

articles.originalTitle: Frieze London 2026 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze London 2026 Opens with Diverse Exhibitions and Boutique Fairs
articles.excerpt: Frieze London and its surrounding events feature new boutique fairs, charity fundraising initiatives, and diverse artistic projects ranging from sculpture to historic queer Modernism.
articles.content:
London's Frieze Week features several new boutique fairs making their debut alongside established events. The Gallery Climate Coalition's '10% Of' fundraising initiative returned to Frieze London for a second year, with 13 galleries pledging a tenth of their proceeds. The PAD London design fair opened its 16th edition with strong sales. Meanwhile, a global collecting survey from Art Basel and UBS indicated that wealthy Gen Z collectors are the art market's largest spenders, with many bypassing traditional dealers to buy directly from artists.

The fair highlights include Frieze Artist Award winner Theo Triantafyllidis's multiplayer video game and spider sculpture. Frieze Masters introduced a curatorial thread exploring the contributions of global LGBTQ+ artists to Modern art. At Tate Modern, artist Tarek Atoui created a sonic installation for the Turbine Hall using bespoke instruments responding to the atrium. Collector Irene Y. Panagopoulos is showing works reflecting on perceptions of Greece at the Hellenic Centre, and Salman Toor's first European solo exhibition opened at the Courtauld Gallery.

Artist Gabrielle Goliath's work 'Elegy', previously barred by the South African government, is being shown by the private foundation Ibraaz. Additionally, the Bagri Foundation launched its first London show featuring Nomin Zezegmaa's batik installation inside a church near Regent's Park, alongside Frieze Sculpture's 11 monumental works.

articles.originalTitle: Carmody Groarke’s Addition to Design Museum Gent Reads as a Manifesto on Sustainable Design - Architectural Record
articles.title: New Sustainable Design Wing Added to Design Museum Gent
articles.excerpt: London-based Carmody Groarke and local practices have designed a five-story extension for Design Museum Gent that serves as a manifesto on sustainable design.
articles.content: Located in Ghent's historic city center, the 23,680-square-foot new wing of Design Museum Gent connects an eclectic complex of historical buildings. Designed by Carmody Groarke with ATAMA and RE-ST, the five-story addition serves as a civic front door. The project features 82,000 Gent Waste Bricks developed with BC Materials, utilizing crushed concrete, glass, and porcelain within a five-mile radius and cured in hydraulic lime to reduce embodied carbon. The architects secured exemptions from local Nearly Energy Neutral standards during pandemic-slowed negotiations. The structure utilizes cross-laminated timber and laminated veneer lumber instead of concrete. Interior features include a 3D-printed recycled aluminum entrance gate and end-grain wood blocks salvaged from a tobacco factory. The top floor houses a free-access public events space overlooking the urban environment.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Explores the Art and Fashion Culture of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain is hosting The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, bringing together art, fashion, photography, and design drawing on curator Edward Enninful's experience.
articles.content: Tate Britain is presenting The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, examining a period defined by bold creativity and a rebellious spirit. Drawing on curator Edward Enninful's experience, the exhibition brings together photography, fashion, art, and design to explore a moment when a new generation transformed culture. The exhibition features works by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Visitors can experience the energy and cultural shifts of a decade that broke down boundaries between art, fashion, and popular culture. Key pieces in the selection include Mark Leckey's video work tracing British dance music culture, Yinka Shonibare's reimagining of colonial histories, and Steve McQueen's silent film Bear. The exhibition is on view from 8 October 2026 to 14 February 2027.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: Mass-Timber East County Library Opens in Oregon Designed by Holst Architecture
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture, the 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, addresses local community needs. The $163 million mass-timber facility serves a rapidly growing population in Multnomah County.
articles.content: Located in Gresham, Oregon, the East County Library was designed by Holst Architecture in collaboration with Adjaye Associates. Spanning 95,000 square feet and built at a cost of $163 million, the facility matches the scale of the 1913 Central Library in downtown Portland. The two-story building stands 59 feet high, serving a region that has experienced significant demographic shifts and population growth since 1994. The design process incorporated extensive community outreach, featuring listening sessions led by five local organizations. The architectural expression utilizes a heavy-timber structural system comprising 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed without additional fire-resistant treatments. Douglas fir was specified for the visible faces of the panels to match the columns and beams. Programmatic spaces include a large auditorium, rooms designed for neurodivergent users, and a recording studio. Mechanical and HVAC systems were positioned in the basement, while ductwork was integrated into the reveals between split-laminated beams to preserve the exposed timber aesthetic throughout the interior.

articles.originalTitle: Boucheron Amps Up Its Spotlight in the U.S. with New Christie’s Exhibition - Robb Report
articles.title: Boucheron Expands United States Presence with Special Exhibition at Christie's New York
articles.excerpt: French high jewelry maison Boucheron is expanding its visibility in the United States with a ten-day exhibition at Christie's New York headquarters, showcasing historical craftsmanship alongside recent contemporary designs.
articles.content: French high jewelry maison Boucheron, founded in 1858, is increasing its engagement in the United States with a ten-day exhibition titled Boucheron: In Focus, a Monograph of a Visionary at Christie's New York headquarters. Following the opening of its North American flagship on Madison Avenue two years ago, the maison aims to present its nearly 170-year history to local clients through archival pieces and loans from private collectors. Organized across thematic sections dedicated to architecture, nature, history, and innovation, the exhibition features notable historical items such as Lady Harcourt's 1924 diamond tiara and Mrs. Mackay's 1888 ruby and diamond collar necklace. Additionally, the presentation includes two recent high jewelry collections, Impermanence and Human Nature, which highlight experimental materials and contemporary techniques directed by creative director Claire Choisne. The exhibition runs from October 9 through October 18 at the auction house's New York venue.

articles.originalTitle: ‘I see the Turbine Hall as a sound vessel’: artist Tarek Atoui on his Tate Modern commission - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Tarek Atoui Creates Sound Installation for Tate Modern Turbine Hall
articles.excerpt: Lebanese artist and composer Tarek Atoui presents his sound-focused installation in the vast Turbine Hall at Tate Modern in London, incorporating bespoke instruments and textiles.
articles.content: Lebanese artist and composer Tarek Atoui has unveiled his sound-focused installation titled Hold in the vast Turbine Hall at Tate Modern in London. The work incorporates bespoke instruments designed to respond to the venue's complex acoustics. Drawing inspiration from the traditional karnai horn of Uzbekistan, Atoui collaborated with the Arthur Mamou-Mani architecture office in London to 3D print horns using a specialized material combining recycled bamboo dust and sugar. He also partnered with the fashion company Issey Miyake to utilize a stretchable textile made from traditional Japanese washi paper and cotton. Coated with charcoal paint, these hanging textiles conduct low-voltage electricity to generate bass sounds through custom synthesizers. Embedded microphones and custom software capture ambient noises and visitor voices within the space, feeding them into a complex processing chain. Atoui notes that human interaction, community engagement, and improvisation with the environment are central to the development of the work, which treats the industrial hall as a sound vessel.

articles.originalTitle: Salman Toor’s Laws of Attraction - ArtReview
articles.title: Salman Toor Exhibition Opens at London's Courtauld Gallery
articles.excerpt: Pakistani-American artist Salman Toor's first institutional exhibition in Europe opens at London's Courtauld Gallery, exploring the thresholds of queer and migrant experiences through narrative paintings.
articles.content: Pakistani-American artist Salman Toor's first institutional exhibition in Europe has opened at London's Courtauld Gallery, featuring nearly 40 paintings and drawings created from 2019 to the present. Curated by Elena Crippa, the exhibition explores themes of belonging, exclusion, and the thresholds shaping queer and migrant experiences. Having relocated from Lahore to the United States in 2002, Toor draws upon personal and communal encounters with strict border controls and racial profiling. Works such as Man with Face Creams and Phone Plug frame immigration checkpoints from the perspective of the authorities, emphasizing the vulnerability of marginalized individuals. In his recent output, Toor incorporates surreal assemblages termed fag puddles, which function as props for code-switching and visual archives reflecting the fatigue and resilience of nonhegemonic bodies navigating hostile social structures. His largest painting to date, The Studio, exhibited at Moderna Museet in Stockholm and referencing Diego Velázquez, incorporates ancestral imagery and ritualistic elements shaped by the artist's reflections during the ongoing conflict in Gaza.

articles.originalTitle: OMA adapts historic houston coffee plant into music and arts academy - Designboom
articles.title: OMA Adapts Historic Houston Coffee Plant into Music and Arts Academy
articles.excerpt: Architecture practice OMA is transforming Houston's 1930s J.A. Folger & Co. coffee plant into the Frank Liu Jr. Academy for Music and Arts.
articles.content: Led by OMA partner Jason Long and project architect Salome Nikuradze, the 6,050-square-meter project is located along Houston’s Buffalo Bayou East corridor. The initiative adapts a historic 1930s industrial building into a tuition-free public charter school focused on music and creative learning. Drawing on Montessori principles, the architecture organizes learning across three stories based on student developmental stages, arranging classrooms around shared commons that OMA terms neighborhoods. To address the challenge of bringing natural light into the industrial structure, classrooms line the perimeter while circular skylights illuminate central shared spaces. The design preserves original industrial elements, including restored street-facing windows and a landscaped courtyard with colorful geometric window divisions. Additional architectural features include a double-height cafetorium and an opening in the floor connecting two libraries shaped like the letter 'f', referencing musical notation and string instruments.

articles.originalTitle: How an Isle of Wight farm building became an architect’s modern-day retreat - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Historic Farm Building on the Isle of Wight Transformed Into Modern Retreat
articles.excerpt: Studio Weave founder Je Ahn has transformed a modest 158 sq m barn on the Isle of Wight into a pared-down personal retreat. Guided by deep reuse, the project preserves original materials while adapting the agricultural structure for modern habitation.
articles.content: Studio Weave practice founder Je Ahn acquired an existing 158 sq m barn within a working farm near Cowes on the UK's Isle of Wight, transforming it into a pared-down personal retreat. Operating with a limited budget and the unique advantage of being his own client, Ahn approached the redesign with an emphasis on flexibility and comfort. The Studio Weave team preserved much of the 50-plus-year-old original fabric, leaving original materials exposed and repairing them to meet 21st-century habitation standards. The heart of the home features a large open-plan kitchen and living area with expansive windows, leading through a small corridor to three bedrooms. Meticulous detailing and craftwork were completed in collaboration with Mike at Imphouse and his team, while the landscape was produced alongside Tom Massey Studio. Grounded in the concept of deep reuse, the design repurposes materials found on site for both their narrative and practical value. The minimal interventions ensure the agricultural building retains its historical integrity while functioning as a contemporary residential space.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.

articles.originalTitle: massimo dutti reincarnates 16th-century palace as rome flagship store - Designboom
articles.title: Massimo Dutti Opens Flagship Store Inside 16th-Century Palazzo Ruspoli in Rome
articles.excerpt: Spanish fashion brand Massimo Dutti has opened a flagship store spanning over 2,000 square meters inside the 16th-century Palazzo Ruspoli in Rome, featuring restored historic architectural details and digital retail services.
articles.content: Spanish fashion brand Massimo Dutti has opened a flagship store within the 16th-century Palazzo Ruspoli along Via del Corso in Rome. Following a heritage study and restoration by specialized artisans, the historic vaulted ceilings, arches, and stone staircase remain visible. Spanning over 2,000 square meters, the retail space features indirect lighting installed at the base of the vaults to highlight the original masonry. The interior design utilizes a material palette centered on wood and fabric for understated sofas and display units. The first floor houses the complete men's and women's collections, marking the debut of the brand's Fall/Winter 2026 Limited Edition. Additional features include an olfactory archive created in collaboration with Florentine perfumery Profumoir, utilizing flame-worked glass holders produced by Pia Glasswork, alongside a curated selection of art and architecture books provided by independent Roman bookstore Leporello Books.

articles.originalTitle: Where 60 Years of Master Craftsmanship Meets Modern Luxury Tech - WWD
articles.title: Adrian Jules Combines HandTailored Craftsmanship With Modern Enterprise Technology
articles.excerpt: Established in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier has developed an enterprise resource planning system to streamline operations in luxury custom clothing.
articles.content: Founded in Rochester, New York, in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier integrates over 60 years of hand-tailored craftsmanship with enterprise technology. The company developed an internal Enterprise Resource Planning system to track garments from initial order entry through workshop cutting, construction, and accounting. The platform serves as a central hub for private-label tailors and retailers, offering real-time visibility into fabric availability, pricing, and high-resolution visuals from global vendors. Platinum division CEO Alex Roberti emphasized the company's commitment to family-run values and high quality, while operations president Arnie Roberti noted that technology has streamlined pattern introduction and inventory tracking. Additionally, Adrian Jules has expanded its offerings by creating pattern designs specifically adapted to women's body shapes, helping retail partners capture a broader luxury market.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Moldova Pavilion: HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Moldova Pavilion Explores the Future in Times of Crisis
articles.excerpt: The Moldova Pavilion in Venice is hosting a roundtable titled HYBRIDREAMS, exploring how to imagine the future amid war and crisis.
articles.content: The Moldova Pavilion, located at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice, is hosting an event exploring how to imagine the future during times of war and crisis. Scheduled for 16 October, the roundtable titled HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis takes its starting point from the country's first official participation in the International Art Exhibition. Organised in collaboration with the European Cultural Foundation and the European Council on Foreign Relations, the programme begins with a church tour. The discussion moves from Moldova's geopolitical realities to examine how political thought, cultural practice, and artistic imagination respond to war and its consequences. The session features former Minister Nicu Popescu, André Wilkens, Silvia Eiblmayr, and Adelina Luft. The conversation aims to address how political and social upheaval calls into question assumptions that previously appeared stable.

articles.originalTitle: The design story behind the breathtaking Shenzhen Natural History Museum - Wallpaper*
articles.title: New Shenzhen Natural History Museum Design Unveiled in China's Pingshan District
articles.excerpt: The Shenzhen Natural History Museum in southern China emerges as a new landmark with undulating architecture inspired by local ecosystems and an accessible rooftop park.
articles.content: Situated on the southern edge of the Pearl River Delta, the Shenzhen Natural History Museum rises amid leafy mounds with an undulating architectural volume. Created by a consortium comprising 3XN, B+H Architects, and Zhubo Design, the facility encompasses 100,000 square meters of exhibition and visitor spaces. Drawing on the subtropical monsoon climate of Pingshan District, the design was conceived not merely as a building, but as a landscape shaped by local geology, water, and time according to 3XN founder Kim Herforth Nielsen. The museum features an accessible rooftop park that serves as a public green space, allowing visitors to walk across zones populated by native and rare plant species. Clad in granite and lamella shingle elements, the curved facade resembles a cliff emerging from the water. The development utilized parametric architectural programmes and digital models to coordinate with the site topography. B+H representatives noted that the structure reflects Shenzhen's ecological richness alongside its rapid urban and technological evolution.

articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Green Building Market Deepens While Navigating Cost and Policy Challenges
articles.excerpt: While sustainable design and contracting revenues are on the rise, industry stakeholders are grappling with challenges such as federal incentive rollbacks, rising costs, and data gaps.
articles.content: Last year, the revenue of the top 100 green design firms increased by 17.1% to $11.8 billion, while international green design revenue rose 18.3% to $2.15 billion. The revenue of the top 100 green contractors also increased by 5.9% to $101.9 billion. While growth varied across markets, the largest increases were observed in industrial processes, hotels, and health care. However, industry experts point out that the rollback of federal sustainability incentives has created a ripple effect on project costs. Jill Kurtz from Stantec notes that many projects face uncertainties regarding real-world performance, emphasizing that decisions should be grounded in building science and operational data rather than certifications alone. Renée Azerbegi of Mead & Hunt states that shifting policy priorities and reduced incentive programs have generated funding uncertainty. Anica Landreneau from HOK reported that clients are increasingly concerned about grid reliability and energy resilience. Contractors suggest that bringing designers and trade partners together early on is critical in translating sustainability goals into practical decisions.

articles.originalTitle: Members' Tour: The Genius of Renaissance Sculptors: Donatello and Michelangelo - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Schedules Members Tour Featuring Donatello and Michelangelo
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting an exclusive members tour exploring the works of Donatello and Michelangelo with a guide. The event takes place on 26 November 2026.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum has announced an exclusive members tour designed to explore the works of Donatello and Michelangelo within its permanent collection. The event is scheduled for Thursday, 26 November 2026, from 15.00 to 16.00 at Blavatnik Hall in V&A South Kensington, London. Tickets are priced at 15.00 pounds, which includes light refreshments served in the Members Room following the tour. Guided by Boe Paschall, the tour examines how both Renaissance sculptors revolutionised and modernised the art form amidst an age of religious and political upheaval. Participants will hear revealing backstories regarding the Protestant Reformation, the extravagance of popes, and church turmoil prompted by nudity. Organisers note that the tour involves extensive walking and stairs, advising members with accessibility questions to contact the events team directly. V&A membership benefits include free entry to exhibitions, dedicated events, and retail discounts.

articles.originalTitle: Peggy Guggenheim Exhibition to Be at the Royal Academy - WWD
articles.title: Royal Academy to Host Peggy Guggenheim Exhibition in London
articles.excerpt: London's Royal Academy of Arts is preparing to host a new exhibition highlighting the history of the Guggenheim Jeune gallery with support from Bottega Veneta.
articles.content: London's Royal Academy of Arts is revisiting the history of the Guggenheim Jeune gallery this fall with a dedicated exhibition. Supported by Bottega Veneta, the show titled "Peggy Guggenheim in London: The Making of a Collector" reexamines the program of the gallery, which staged over 20 exhibitions in under a year before closing in June 1939. The venue's original run included Vasily Kandinsky's first solo show in the United Kingdom, Britain's inaugural collage exhibition, and a sculpture presentation. The upcoming presentation features works by Eileen Agar, Salvador Dalí, Barbara Hepworth, Rita Kernn-Larsen, Henry Moore, Piet Mondrian, Cedric Morris, and Sophie Taeuber-Arp. Many of these pieces are returning to London for the first time since their debut. Bottega Veneta stated that the partnership reflects its roots in Venice and its commitment to craftsmanship, experimentation, and creative freedom. The exhibition will run from November 21 through March 14, before traveling to the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York in April.

articles.originalTitle: Cosima von Bonin’s soft toys storm the Petit Palais - Art Basel
articles.title: Cosima von Bonin Unveils Dollys & Beaux Exhibition at Petit Palais
articles.excerpt: German artist Cosima von Bonin presents the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais for Art Basel Paris's public program, bringing together her fabric sculptures and soft toy figures.
articles.content: Kenyan-born German artist Cosima von Bonin is presenting the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais as part of Art Basel Paris's public program. The exhibition features large-scale soft-stuffed leather, velvet, and mohair sculptures created by the artist. These figures, which previously appeared in Loewe's Fall/Winter 2026 collection show, establish a dialogue between contemporary art and fashion. The presented works include velvet St. Bernard dog sculptures with plush barrels around their necks, sea scallops, a hermit crab, an octopus, and a killer whale. Spanning a career of over 40 years, von Bonin's installations encourage open-ended interpretations from viewers rather than imposing a single narrative. Miu Miu serves as the official partner for the public program. Dollys & Beaux is on view at the Petit Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026, while Art Basel Paris takes place at the Grand Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: In Transit with artist Nour Jaouda - Art Basel
articles.title: Exploring Space, Memory, and Movement with Artist Nour Jaouda
articles.excerpt: In an interview as part of the In Transit series produced in partnership with Qatar Airways, Libyan artist Nour Jaouda discusses how travel, memory, and cultural mobility shape her textile and sculptural practices.
articles.content: Working with sculptural, hand-dyed textiles and hanging fiber installations, Libyan artist Nour Jaouda explores how spaces embody memory. Based between Cairo and London, Jaouda notes that moving between diverse social and cultural landscapes has informed her visual language. A 2023 visit to Benghazi, where she reconnected with a decades-old fig tree in her grandmother's garden, directly influenced her tapestries created for the 2024 Venice Biennale. Explaining that carrying a prayer mat during travels grounds her, she emphasizes the importance of this ritual. Connecting color to movement, Jaouda employs deconstruction and décollage techniques to create meaning through unmaking and restructuring. In Cairo, she finds inspiration in the architectural layers of Downtown, while in London, she prefers walking aimlessly to discover subtle moments. At Art Basel Qatar, her installation A House Between Two Houses presented a space shaped by emotional subjectivity and memory rather than fixed geography, engaging with concepts of transformation and decay. Watching the fair come to life in Doha and meeting fellow creators provided her with an insightful experience rooted in a rich history.

articles.originalTitle: Yohji Yamamoto Drawings - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts Talk on Unpublished Yohji Yamamoto Drawings
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host an event celebrating a collection of previously unpublished drawings by designer Yohji Yamamoto.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a special talk and book celebration on Wednesday 9 December to mark the publication of Yohji Yamamoto Drawings. Author and curator Alexandre Samson will join Yohji Yamamoto's executive advisor, Caroline Fabre, at V&A South Kensington to discuss a collection of never-before-published drawings selected by Yamamoto himself. Featuring menswear and womenswear sketches designed with support from Peter Saville, the book offers insight into the designer's creative process and his exploration of fashion and form. Samson and Fabre will discuss Yamamoto's creative practice and the enduring legacy of his work during the evening event, which includes a wine reception and book signing. Priority booking for members is open, with general ticket sales beginning on 19 October, subject to availability. Ticket prices range from 15.00 to 20.00 pounds and include the post-talk reception.

articles.originalTitle: Painting large as an Impressionist: Renoir and the full-length format | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery Examines Renoir and Full-Length Portraiture
articles.excerpt: Colin B. Bailey, Director of The Morgan Library and Museum, will deliver a special lecture at the National Gallery's Pigott Theatre exploring Pierre-Auguste Renoir's large-scale portraits.
articles.content: The National Gallery is hosting a special event focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's full-length portraits, recognized among the most ambitious works of his career. Held in conjunction with the exhibition Renoir and Love, the lecture features Colin B. Bailey, Katharine J. Rayner Director of The Morgan Library & Museum, who will examine how the artist captured modern life, emotions, and social interactions in 19th-century Paris. Drawing on decades of research into eighteenth- and nineteenth-century French art, Bailey will explore Renoir's technical brilliance, evolving portraiture approach, and psychological immediacy. The talk will take place in the Pigott Theatre on Level -1 of the Sainsbury Wing. Standard tickets are priced at 10 pounds, while concessions are available at 8 pounds for full-time students, jobseekers, and disabled adults. Advance booking is required for attendance, and members will have the option to join the event online. This lecture offers audiences a distinct opportunity to closely examine the artist's celebrated figures within the broader context of friendship, love, and modernity explored throughout the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Renoir and Love | Exhibitions - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery in London Opens Major Renoir and Love Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition exploring the artist's depiction of human connections and everyday emotions through 40 paintings gathered from international collections, on view until January 31, 2027.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's exploration of love, friendship, and human connection during his peak period from the 1860s to the 1880s. Running until January 31, 2027, the exhibition brings together 40 paintings from collections across the world, highlighting the artist's role as an innovator of Impressionism. Notably, Renoir's iconic 1876 painting Bal au Moulin de la Galette from the Musée d'Orsay is on display in the United Kingdom for the first time. The exhibition is organized jointly by the Musée d'Orsay, the National Gallery, and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Visitors can explore sun-dappled gardens, dance halls, and intimate everyday moments captured by the artist, with flexible pay-what-you-wish admission options available on select Friday evenings.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, marking the artist's first retrospective in New York since 1993 and gathering roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art in New York hosts Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the artist's first major retrospective in the city since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein's early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works produced from the early 1940s to the 1990s, the exhibition explores his treatment of images as unstable forms subject to borrowing, translation, and reframing. For the first time, all works from Lichtenstein's inaugural Pop-style exhibition at the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended its impact beyond Pop art, shaping subsequent generations of artists whose works are also displayed within the exhibition.
